summary: Walther Schubring was an Indologist who studied at the universities of Munich, Strasbourg (PhD under Ernst Leumann), and Berlin (Habilitation). He held posts at the Royal Library of Berlin, Humboldt University of Berlin, and the University of Hamburg (1920–1951).

Walther Wüst was an Indologist and linguist who completed his PhD at the University of Munich in 1923. He held Munich posts from 1926 to 1945, and served at the Ahnenerbe (1936) and the Deutsche Akademie (1943).

Wanda Dynowska worked in religious studies, Indology, and Tibetology, and studied at the University of Lausanne. She served as general secretary of the Polish Theosophical Society in 1921 and founded the Indo-Polish Library in 1944.
Wang Pachow was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology who studied under Tan Yun-shan. He served on the teaching and research staff at Visva-Bharati University.

Wannaporn Rienjang is a historian, archaeologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Cambridge. Her career includes roles at the British Museum, Classical Art Research Centre, Thammasat University, and University of Oxford.

Warren Crawford Cowgill was a linguist and Indologist who earned his BA at Stanford and his PhD at Yale under Paul Tedesco and Paul Thieme. He served on the faculty at Yale University as Assistant Professor from 1956 to 1972.

Warren Lee Todd works in philosophy and Indology. He earned his PhD at Lancaster University under the doctoral supervision of Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad, and also studied under Irina Kuznetsova, Peter Harvey, and Chogye Trichen Rinpoche.

Warrin Ratanamalai is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, supervised by Phra Suthithammanuwat and Phra Srisitthimuni, and also studied under Phra Sudhivorayan and Somjin Sammāpañño.

Waso Harada works in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied at Ryukoku University and Koyasan University. He held positions at Koyasan University, Toseiji, Ryukoku University, and Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College.

Watari Yanai was a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1898 to 1901 and later held a post there from ~1908 to 1926.

Wataru Mori worked in philosophy and other fields. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1947 to 1951, later holding academic posts at Tokyo Medical and Dental University (~1968–1973) and the University of Tokyo (~1973–1989).

Wataru Ryose is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1987 under the doctoral supervision of Minoru Kiyota, having also studied under Genjun Sasaki and Frances Wilson.
Wayne Chandira works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He pursued doctoral studies in religious studies at McMaster University under the supervision of Mark Rowe.

Wayne Proudfoot is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned his Master of Theology and PhD at Harvard University. He taught at Fordham University (~1970–1972) and became Professor of Religion at Columbia University around 1972.

Wei Lin is an archaeologist and Sinologist who studied at Nanjing University, Peking University, and Ohio State University (PhD under John C. Huntington). He held posts at Nanjing Municipal Museum, Ohio State, Western Michigan, Michigan, and Transylvania University.
Wei Wu is a Buddhist studies scholar who founded the International Buddhist College. She also served as Associate Professor and Director of Undergraduate Studies at Emory University.

Wei-Cheng Lin is a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He held a professorship at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill until 2015, when he joined the faculty at the University of Chicago.

Wei-jen Teng, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies, studied at the University of Chicago and Harvard (PhD). He has held posts at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts and Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Wei-ming Tu is a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and religious studies. Educated at Tunghai and Harvard (PhD), he held faculty posts at Princeton, UC Berkeley, and Harvard, and directed the Harvard-Yenching Institute from 1996 to 2008.
Weijue Shi was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Lingshuan and Lingyuan. He founded the Lin Quan Temple in 1987, the Chung Tai Buddhist Institute in 1993, and Chung Tai Shan.
